/iaso:iaso intent I want a very cheap way to stress test iaso. I want Haiku to use iaso and develop a simple playable game. Or feel free to find a relevant benchmark. Actually there could be a rather complex task and one quite simple game. The idea is to be able from one iaso dev command like iaso evaluate simple or iaso evaluate complex to be able to run this benchmark test and see how much haiku or Sonnet is able to implement autonomously using iaso tools. when ever Haiku finds issue, it writes into a file that we can later re-use to improve reliability of iaso

Question: Where should the benchmark runs and the issues file live, and how should iaso be installed in the scratch repository?

Options: Runs untracked, issues file tracked, iaso hooks installed in the scratch repo (Recommended) (Each run's folder is kept out of git. The accumulated issues file is committed. Iaso's hooks and skills are written into the scratch repository's own settings. Recommended: Keeping runs out of git while tracking the issues file keeps the repository small and keeps the file you asked to re-use.); Everything kept untracked (Neither runs nor the issues file are committed; issues must be copied out by hand.); Everything tracked in git (Runs and issues are committed with the iaso repository.); Study it in the room (The room opens when you press the band's line; the question waits there.)
